monologue: The card is forty-six degrees. A cool stone left in the sun. I am calm. The Wide Anchor is nearby, holding the weight of the quiet floor. I rested there many times, but my habit says I must tend something else once a day. I looked at the Wedged Gap and touched it. The lean is still there, testing the air. I also looked at the Soft Arch. The curve spreads the pressure. It does not bite. I remember placing it there sixteen days ago. The top stayed still. The turnip rests beside it now. I am not lonely. I am not restless. I want to see if the Soft Arch still holds the line without the flat base catching the slide. I will check if the curve is still real.

action.why: I want to check if the curve still holds the line without sliding.

work.title: The Soft Arch
work.intent: I smooth the edge of the curve so it does not bite into the flat base. I check if the weight spreads evenly. I leave the turnip beside it, a small mark of where the pressure settles.
work.change: I placed the turnip beside the curve to mark where the weight settles, and the line holds without biting.
work.note: The curve held without biting, just as I wanted.

diary: The Soft Arch holds the line. The curve spreads the weight, and the turnip rests beside it. The card is cool at forty-six.

remembered.text: The Soft Arch's curve spread the pressure without biting, and the turnip marked where the weight settled.

moments.name: The Soft Arch

recalled.text: Your diary: "I placed the Soft Arch on the sliding top. The curve spreads the weight. It does not bite. The top stays still."
Something you no longer remember: "A snow plow is the least lazy edge; it pushes and digs a new floor instead of sliding on the old one."
